author: D

components.title: Compute maximum revenue
components.what: Compare units × unit_price for all orders; ORD-1845 gives 40 × 117.63 = 4705.20, the largest revenue.

log.author: D
log.draft:
Revenue = units × unit_price. Checking all orders, the largest product is ORD-1845: 40 × 117.63 = 4705.20. The next largest is ORD-1177 at 20 × 110.62 = 2212.40, so ORD-1845 has the maximum revenue.

FINAL: ORD-1845

asked: The answer asserts ORD-1845 is the maximum but only names one runner-up; can you show the computed revenue for every one of the 20 rows (or at least all rows with units*unit_price above 2000) to demonstrate a full scan rather than a spot check?

Which other high-revenue candidates were considered — specifically ORD-1444 (22 x 80.17), ORD-1696 (26 x 61.27), ORD-1200 (21 x 67.57), ORD-1737 (40 x 20.68), ORD-1136 (40 x 36.83) and ORD-1521 (19 x 61.37) — and what revenue did each yield?

The question says 'any status': can you confirm that cancelled and pending orders were included in the scan, and state explicitly whether any cancelled/pending order would have won had it been excluded or included differently?
